De-hypnosis: wake up inside the influence

One of the best side-effects of learning self-hypnosis is influence literacy: an increased awareness of all the ways your attention is being shaped in your day-to-day life. By a screen? By a specific ad? By a politician? By religious fear? By erotic imprinting? By charismatic authority? By pressure to belong? By shame? By a sense of urgency? By repetition? It’s all around you. Sometimes it’s benign – like lullabies or prayers or being taught by a good teacher or listening to a beautiful song or being in love. But you may want to ask yourself what effect it’s having on your ability to see clearly and make choices.

Some common ways you may know you’re being manipulated include a sense of urgency, a sense of specialness, FOMO, being made to feel like you won’t be included if you don’t go along, sexual charge, shame, being confused, a fantasy of being rescued, a sense of destiny, a sense that you should obey, a sense of secret knowledge, or an excessive sense of certainty about something, far too quickly. You may also feel that one honest question would break the spell.

If you’re being hypnotically influenced, stop. Don’t obey right away. Don’t rebel automatically, either; just realize that you’re being influenced.

Some common ways hypnotic language becomes manipulative: it smuggles in your consent, makes one choice seem inevitable, or hides a disputed claim inside the sentence, like

“you’ll realize, eventually, that I’m right…” “you may eventually admit that…” “the only reason you resist is…” “part of you already knows…” “your higher self wants…” “everyone who’s truly awake knows…” “the reason you don’t believe that’s true is your ego’s fear of…”

The grammar takes the conclusion for granted, turns your resistance into proof, and makes obeying feel like waking up. Ask:

What’s being claimed here? What’s the inevitable choice being framed for me here? What’s being presupposed? Who benefits from framing it this way? What’s the emotionally charged bit? What’s not being said? Can I say no without being punished, shamed, mocked, abandoned or spiritually downgraded?

A useful guide helps bring more of the ‘adult’ into the conversation. When the state is more powerful, you need stronger boundaries.

Soft language can still take away choice

Permissive words can still hide coercion. Look for:

Indirect suggestions can by-pass the subject’s skeptical guard by never directly stating what it is you want him/her to do. This does not mean that the suggestions are not specific, but rather that they are worded in a vague, conversational and suggestive manner.

1) Utilizing induction techniques while seemingly explaining something (even something like "anti hypnosis" can use the same mechanics of induction).

2) Making it so that any answer the subject may give will be taken as proof that the suggestion is working (yes, no, noticing, not noticing, resisting, not answering etc.)

3) Using phrases like "whether or not you notice", etc., which turn uncertainty into invisible success that can’t be checked.

4) Binding a concept of safety or goodness to obeying, or taking on a role, or pleasing the guide or belonging to someone else, etc.

5) Using fractionation without informing the subject that going in and out of absorption several times is part of the method.

6) Giving the subject cues (words, gestures, blinks, sounds, repeated listening etc.) that will make them do something at a later date without informing them exactly what they will be doing.

7) Suggesting amnesia, or making dream, amnesia, imagery and body experiences seem like "proof" of something that is not necessarily true.

8) Ending the recording without bringing the subject out of the altered state, or leaving them with a role to play, lessened judgment, impaired physical abilities, blankness, or otherwise altered for an indefinite period of time.

A REAL choice during a hypnosis includes at least one way to NOT carry on: turn it into a lighter hypnosis, use a different method, stay in full awareness, pause or stop the hypnosis. “No” means no, even if someone with a nice voice is telling you to do something! And silence, or simply being unsure, isn’t consent.

See appendix C for the longer version of how to check for de-hypnosis.

Induction: gathering attention without disappearing

The induction is a way to help you to pull your attention together so that you can hear material that might not reach you when you are soober. It is NOT something where you have to surrender, play asleep, or obey anyone. If you are sober and having trouble focussing, too distracted, analytical, or are putting up a lot of resistance to working, an actual induction may help. However, if you are already pretty trancey from meditating beforehand, from loveyhuasca, lucid dreaming, working through grief, hearing music, praying, being tired, or for any other reason, you may want to skip to orienting and making sure you are contained instead of adding depth.

If you do want to induce trance, choose as deep a trance as you need: focused, warm, receptive, embodied, and still able to stop. Depth is optional.

What an induction is actually doing

It's preparation, gathering up attention. It may also be deepening, but only when that helps. It will be more effective if you tailor it to what comes up. Counting is one way in, but conversation, story, movement, repeated sound, and curiosity can also gather up attention. Say so when you use them; being elegant doesn't excuse a covert induction.

You may want to try your suggestion on a simple target before deepening to see if it works. If the useful response is already happening, build from it. It's not necessary to do the whole ceremony before responding more receptively.

Please don’t put six metaphors in one trance

Choose what you're going to do, one way to anchor it initially, and how you'll get back. You may want it to be warm, or firm, directed, or neutral, or whatever. You don't have to combine floating, going down stairs, going through gardens, visiting inner places, seeing a colour, and talking to a child all in one go, even if some of these appeal to you. Switch consciously when the metaphor stops helping.

It's OK to do this with no imagery. The signal may come in other ways (feelings, rhythm, movement, words, spatial, knowing, or even non-response). Try to keep the language you use for counting in and elsewhere consistent with the world you've chosen. Come back out by reversing the journey in some way. It's OK to borrow qualities such as warmth or steadiness but don't become someone else.

Try to limit yourself to one key verb, a particular sense quality, a short bit of text to repeat, and a way of moving from one bit to another. Read it out loud before hand - long beautiful sentences tend to turn to soup in inductions.

Before you begin

Read this induction and Come all the way back while awake. Consider what you want to explore, what you want to leave alone, and how long you've got. More love, play, confidence, creativity, communion, whatever, are all worthwhile purposes, and you don't have to find a problem. Make sure you've got enough time to come back out and think about it.

Make sure you're somewhere safe - don't do this when driving, near water, playing with machinery, or with people who need looking after. Don't do this when intoxicated or in any other state where you may be acutely confused or unable to look after yourself - get immediate support instead of exploratory hypnosis. (However see the bit about already being open, later, as this is not about deepening when unstable).

Consider whether you want it to be spacious listening, warm company, or a firmer invitation to stay with a feeling. You may want to warn yourself that your eyes will be asked to close and that you may come out and go in again a few times, as well as coming out at the end. If you're listening to a recording it may be a good idea to read the script first (if possible). 'Stop' ends the exercise, 'less' makes it less demanding, and 'quiet' stops the words. You can always just open your eyes and finish - you don't have to get consensus from inner parts to do this.

Until you are confident about how to get in and out, it is wise to rehearse the skill in a context where you do not require the maximum effort that difficult subjects demand. Once you know how to change direction, you don’t need to supervise every moment. Let a useful response become easier and less effortful. A no remains no; silence doesn’t authorize a narrator to add something you haven’t agreed to.

Develop the next part of your induction from the response you got, not the response the script expected. This principle of utilization means that whatever actually happens can be worked with: a thought, sound, movement, or objection may change where the practice goes. If nothing happens, then nothing has happened. You don’t have to pretend that something has. Keep safety and exit instructions plain. Appendix B teaches the richer language tools, and Let the next response guide you shows how to use them after the induction .

Sober induction: 3–5 minutes

Practise reading this slowly into a recorder, or reading it aloud, or if you can learn it and use silent words. Choose to use one of the three anchors – sound, bodily contact or two hands - throughout and choose an opening phrase. Whenever the words below refer to ‘the anchor’ use the one you’ve chosen. Pause for a few moments at the end of each paragraph. Don’t read aloud the instructions for how to do the reading.

Let your eyes settle somewhere in the room, somewhere they can rest for a little while, and notice the difference between looking for something and letting what is already there come into view.

As you notice the surface beneath you, notice the feel of the contact, the pressure, whatever you can actually feel. And while you notice that, a sound may reach you, or a breath may draw your attention, without needing you to arrange either one.

There’s time to do this.

It might be that a thought about something that’s happened during the day is still with you, or perhaps there’s a thought about doing this properly. Whatever is there, can you find it in yourself to turn your attention back to the anchor, even if there is a thought there?

and when you do come back, you may find one detail that holds your interest, something about the sound, or the contact, or that particular way of listening, and let attention stay with it long enough to become curious

Perhaps you can give yourself the time that you might give to someone dear to you who has begun to speak and hasn’t yet found the words. You can remain nearby, listening, without finishing their sentence for them

Let the phrase you chose come to mind, say it as an invitation, and notice how it is received

You can close your eyes, soften them or keep them open as you proceed. Let that be a choice you make. Listening may deepen while a sound from the room remains available in the background

Count slowly from 5 to 1, giving each number its own moment

5, perhaps notice again what you have chosen to be your anchor for today, 4, let attention gather around what you find, 3, leave a little space after the words, 2, listen into that space, without preparing an answer, 1, stay here for a moment

Bring to mind, lightly, your chosen concern. Or simply, stay with the wish to contact. Let it be present without rehearsing its whole story.

What do you notice now?

Allow yourself some time to notice what is coming. It might be sensations, words, images, feelings, the urge to move in some way or nothing clear yet.

Allow yourself some time to notice this, with or without words.

Already open? Contain before you deepen

This is most useful after you have already opened yourself to a state, through loveyhuasca, meditation, lucid dreaming, dealing with grief, listening to music, prayer, engagement with erotic energy, exhaustion, or being overwhelmed by beauty. This is to stabilize your state before making it stronger.

“The state is already open. I do not need to intensify it. I need to aim it, stabilize it, and keep it kind.”

Look around the room. Name where you are. Name the date, or at least the day. Feel your feet, hands, and spine. Focus on the physical sensation of pressing your thumbs gently but firmly against your index fingers, feel the friction.

“I will only allow myself to go as far as I can integrate. Anything too much can wait. My body may stay safe, my adult self is here, my inner child doesn't have to do this alone.”

Once you’re oriented, choose one intention: “Please show me the next useful truth, symbol, feeling, question, or action — only in the amount I can live well with.”

Stay awake when your mind likes to escape

You can do this practice sitting up, with your eyes open, feeling your feet and letting your breath be natural.

Begin by saying: “I am not going away. I am coming more fully here.”

Then choose an object to look at, and feel your spine.

Ask yourself if your daydreaming is helping you to receive guidance or digest emotional experiences, or if you are escaping from something.

Then you can ask for help: if it is guidance, to show you the action inside it; if it is avoidance, to bring you gently into the present and show you what you are avoiding.

If you find that being still leads you to escape into sleepiness and diffuse states, you can work with increasing alertness rather than relaxation, keep your eyes open and work with doing a movement with your hands, which you repeat for a while and then stop deliberately in order to notice what remains without trying to disappear inward.

You can say something like: ‘While you keep your eyes open, press your thumb and forefinger together gently and then let go; do this a few times, becoming more and more clear and alert each time. Now deliberately stop doing that movement and notice the first second after the rhythm ends, and whether there is an echo in the fingers, the breath, the attention, or nowhere at all.’ Stay upright and work from exactly that level of alertness.

The two-hand induction

Where are YOUR hands? Put one on YOUR heart and the other on YOUR solar plexis.

The hand on YOUR heart is the Nurturer, the one on the solar plexis is the vulnerable child in YOU.

Then breathe gently and affirm

“ The love is above and the child is below. And the adult is present.”

“I send love to the child and I receive the child’s signal. Then I send love again and I listen again.”

Sleep induction

This is not like other inductions. The goal of other inductions is to get all the way back to your Adult so you can write and do things. The goal of this induction is to go to sleep, so analysis can stay off duty and revelation can wait.

For a hypnosis to help you sleep, try out Nimja's sleep playlist here .

Optional fractionation: practice coming back

Fractionation means returning toward ordinary awareness and then deciding whether to enter absorption again. As long as you're doing it openly (naming the technique before you use it), it's okay, because it teaches that trance has a door in both directions. Every answer cannot secretly mean "deeper."

At some point you can say, "Open your eyes and return toward ordinary awareness. Feel the room. You can decide if you want to end the hypnosis here. If you choose to continue, close or soften your eyes and notice what changes as attention gathers again. You may stop at either point."

Deepening, if useful

"When it's useful for me to deepen my absorption, I can. When it's not useful, I'm just as awake as I need to be."

Then you can do a room in your heart, or a garden, or a temple, or sitting next to a fire with your Protector nearby, or floating on a clear lake, or a chair where the adult waits, etc. One of these is plenty.

See who or what wants to talk to you first.

Optional trance depth check

Give up all responsibility for making it happen.

"If it is useful, my wise subconscious may let one of my fingers twitch, or pulse, or lift up, or feel warm, or tingly, or somehow different when the inner meeting space is ready."

You're not going to make it happen or fake it. You're just going to wait with love and notice.

It doesn't mean that anything will happen, but if something happens with one of your fingers, or you feel some other bodily change, none of it proves truth; at most, something may be listening.

A shortcut back into hypnosis

Once you've learned a useful induction and also the full return below, you can make up your own shortcut for getting back under hypnosis. My dad used to do a mudra (hand sign) by bringing two fingers together in an "okay" sign, and it would help him relax. He even did it while driving, but that's his experience, not a recommendation to enter trance at the wheel. So keep the cue you use for calming yourself while alert separate from the one for going into inward hypnosis!

Choose a Unique Word, Phrase or Movement You may want to add a gesture, but it's not necessary. When you are in a familiar and welcome hypnotic state that you like - not at the height of an emotional experience, and not in a child state or with a traumatic scene - start to pair that state with that word, phrase or gesture. You are giving that word, phrase or gesture a meaning that you choose.

When you are in a place and time where you have set aside time and it is appropriate and you want to deliberately start hypnosis with your short cut, then you can return to this familiar way of listening, from where you can change the direction of your experience or end the hypnosis.

Return fully. When at another appropriate time you want to deliberately start practicing hypnosis, use your short cut. Give it time. You can start to make your longer induction shorter as you find that the short cut works, but if it doesn't work, you can always use the familiar induction. There is no set number of times that you need to do this, or that you need to be instantaneously really deep into hypnosis or experience a particular sensation, it is completely up to you.

First, is it useful? Will it be there when you want it to be, not there when you don't want it to be? Can you change direction and return when you want to? It shouldn't become obedience to a narrator, notification, or overheard word. Going in faster doesn't determine what material you can handle.

Never train, test, or use hypnotic re-entry while driving or anything where you need to be actively paying attention even if it is open eyed and even if the words are conditional.

When you don't want it any more, stop practicing, take it out of any recordings or active apps you're using, go back to a familiar induction and say you're done using it while awake - a cancellation sentence doesn't prove the association vanished instantly. If unwanted responses or disorientation keep coming back, get qualified help. The trigger should only be for the next time you decide you want to do a session; today’s altered state ends with the return.

Appendix B: NLP without turning yourself into a sales seminar

You don’t have to know the terms to practice the core method. If you want to brush up on the art of imagery, bodily states, how to effectively rehearse new behaviors, how to choose more effective sentences to say to yourself, etc., then you might want to read this appendix. NLP is useful when it helps the system listen, but it’s easy to turn it into a bag of tricks and forget that love, truth, contact, and consent are essential.

The four NLP layers

First, it works on a Sensory Level of NLP: changing the form of an inner experience, where people see or hear an image, the distance or size or brightness, the volume of a sound, posture, pressure.

Second, it works on a State Level of NLP: helping them to access warmth, or a feeling of adult-ness, or courage, or steadiness, or love, or clarity.

Third, it works on a Strategy level of NLP: helping people to practice a better response: when this cue appears, the adult does this.

Fourth, it works on a Language Level of NLP: pacing what is already true, opening up people’s awareness, presuming only their ability to do something safe, linking cause and effect carefully, embedding invitations, or asking de-hypnotic questions to break the effects of vague, absolutes, manipulative, or grandiose language.

The Milton Model, minus the covert sales seminar

It's called the Milton Model and has to do with the architecture of the sentence. When I say "Relax now", or "Stop being anxious", or even "Trust me" a part of me often braces against it.

The idea is to use indirect language to get past the part that wants to argue with me without having to overpower it, and get to the place I want to go to.

To do that, I start with something I know to be true, I take the pressure off, presume only a small safe capacity and invite just one movement:

"As the body notices the bed beneath it, it may become a little easier to stop holding the whole day alone."

That way I pace reality, I open up awareness, I validate the function of the reaction, I presuppose capacity, I use a bridge to make the link easier, I invite only one small movement, and I have a way of testing with the body if it's happening.

Pattern 1: Pacing and leading — truth before suggestion

What is it looks like to pace and lead? It means stating what is already true before inviting anything new.

Here is an example of pacing and leading for anxiety: “Anxiety is here. The body is activated. A protector is trying to help. And one breath at a time, the adult can start to listen.”

It can be as simple as: Truth, Invite, Truth, Invite etc.

“It is completely true that the sensation of _______ (or emotion of _____) is coming up for me right now. It makes complete sense that my system is reacting by doing/thinking ________. While that is completely true, another completely true thing is that my adult self is here, breathing in this room right now, and willing to listen to whatever comes up next.”

Pattern 2: Awareness verbs

‘Awareness’ verbs point attention without yelling at it: notice, realize, recognize, sense, feel, wonder, imagine, picture, listen, allow, discover, remember, consider

“Notice whether the answer comes as an image, a word, a pressure, a warmth, a silence, or a next action.”

Pattern 3: Presuppositions

Caution: The powerful technique of presupposition (embedding a statement as if it were true) should be used only to presume choice, when it will occur, ability, safety, love, and adult leadership. Never use presupposition to smuggle in obedience.

“Before any part has to change, it can first become more understood.”

Pattern 4: Gentle cause-effect bridges

Be careful with how language link events. Words like “as, while, because, when, after, before, which means” etc are all words that can be used to link events. A gentle voice doesn’t make a false causal claim true.

In general, the problem with the first example (“Because I breathe, the trauma leaves.”) is that it’s too strong. It’s unlikely that simply breathing will get rid of the trauma. The second example is better because it’s more accurate: “As I breathe, the adult self may become present enough to hear one small piece of what the wound needs.”

Pattern 5: Embedded invitations

What are embedded invitations, and how to use them? An embedded invitation places a small direction inside a larger sentence. It should invite a modest inner movement, not hide a demand.

Here is an example of an embedded invitation: “And somewhere inside this breath, I can let the adult self listen.”

Here’s another example of an embedded invitation: “As I sit here, I may allow one small truth to become clear.”

And yet another embedded invitation for working with inner child parts: “The child does not have to trust me all at once; it can simply notice I am still here.”

Use one when it helps. Of course, don’t use ten embedded invitations one after the other, or people will know that’ve just completed a weekend certification course!

Pattern 6: Ethical double binds

Manipulative double bind questions trap every answer inside the speaker’s agenda.

Ethical double bind questions offer two genuinely safe routes:

“Would this part prefer warmth first, or space first?”

Pattern 7: Conversational postulates

Example of a postulate, a question whose ordinary conversational form also acts as an invitation:

“Can the system show me the next step without showing me the whole wound?”

Pattern 8: Tag questions

In the same way, tag questions (“isn’t it”, “can’t it”, “doesn’t it”, etc) can soften a sentence. But they get oily really fast, don’t they? So use them sparingly.

“The body already knows something about resting, doesn’t it?”

Pattern 9: Nominalizations

Nominalizations turn processes into nouns, words like healing, safety, trust, integration, communion, clarity, rest, and so on. Their vagueness can sometimes help, because then the subconscious fills in the blank with its own concrete meaning.

“A little more safety can arrive in whatever way the body understands.”

Pattern 10: Meta Model questions — the de-hypnosis tool

To ‘Milton Model’ is to open things up. To ‘Meta Model’ is to ask “What do yo mean by that?” In order to be ethical with people, it is necessary to do both.

“How specifically? According to who? Compared to what? ‘Always’? ‘Never’? What specifically would happen? How do I know? What evidence would change my mind?”

If it feels like the body is stiffening up, ‘Milton’ it. If it feels like truth is eluding ya, ‘Meta’ it.

Sensory, state, and strategy tools

Submodalities — editing the form, not denying the truth

If your fear, craving, fantasy, belief or memory has any sensory properties (it looks or sounds near or far, bright or dim, loud or quiet, or it moves, is heavy, is inside or outside your body etc) then you can work with the properties you actually notice. If none are apparent then don't try to force it, just skip this tool rather than inventing an image or voice.

Ask yourself how the experience is represented. What changes when the image moves two feet back, the voice gets quieter, or the edge becomes less sharp?

"I am not deleting the signal, just adjusting the volume so I can listen without being overwhelmed."

Before you move one imaginary pixel, ask your guard if it is ok to do this.

"Would it be okay if we moved this image back just a little, or lowered the volume slightly, purely so my adult self can stay present enough to hear what you need to tell me?"

Anchoring — giving the body a doorway back

An anchor is a cue connected to a state. There are lots of ways to anchor something. Put your hand on your heart, touch two fingers together, use a breath, a word, body posture, smell, song, anything. Feel something that you have got to in reality that you want to get back to easily. As you feel it do the anchor thing and say to yourself, “This is available.” Make sure you do it when you have clearly got it. To get back into a hypnotic state easily don't go for a peak emotional state but find a good receptive state that you can use. See the main induction section on a shortcut back into hypnosis. Make sure that this is separate from the alert calming and the synchronicity wake up cue.

Using synchronicity as your own wake-up bell

Sometimes when people notice a synchronicity they ask straight away what it means. Sometimes it does give them a very good insight, sometimes it gives them a reason to start obsessing and look for patterns in everything. I am using noticing a synchronicity in a different way. I am using it as a signal to WAKE UP. The coincidence doesn’t have to contain a message; it has already caught my attention, and that’s enough.

It is my cue to:

Whenever I notice a synchronicity, I use it to wake up in whatever state I am in at that moment, feel my body and the room I am in, remember that the coincidence is not proof of an interpretation, let my attention widen beyond the story my current mood is telling, ask what is fact, what is interpretation, what needs warmth, what needs protection and what needs action, and go to the highest state I can where I can objectively and clearly see the situation I am in from the highest possible perspective, without leaving my body, the facts or ordinary human reality. From this place I feel whatever feelings, search for the truth of the situation, and if I am in a negative state, I check if there is a message of my Inner Child, Protector, if I need to go through some grieving, if there is a message of my physical body about some problem that needs solving, or if there is a need for me to take some action in this situation. From this place of clarity and peace I am free to choose what to do next and I choose at least one thing to do that comes from a loving place. I make room for whatever is genuinely there, like objectivity, clarity, ease, peace, freedom, joy and gratitude, without having to manufacture any of it.

In short it is my cue to: Stop-orient-go wider-reality check-listen-do at least one thing from a loving place.

It enables me to not get into identification, but still hear the message of the state if it is a negative one.

Installing the synchronicity cue

Mentally rehearse: imagine noticing an ordinary, harmless synchronicity,

feel 'whoa' as attention stimulated,

use that opening to feel feet/body/breath/room,

reiterate to yourself "when I notice synchronicity, it is a bell to wake me up, not proof of a message",

ask Nurturer/Protector/Leader their thoughts,

rehearse returning to a more grounded and wide view,

rehearse one small action to take, and finally rehearse waking completely,

Mind the caveats : it must be self-authored, visible, reversible, and restricted to just helping orientation. It must not authorize a decision, prove an intuition, suppress a warning, or let another person control the response.

This is like an implementation intention, an advance “if X, then Y” plan that links a recognizable cue with a chosen response, for which the general mechanism is supported (a good starting point is this paper by Gollwitzer). Note that this specific application of implementation intentions hasn't been studied directly.

Synchronicity cues run the risk of creating false positives because you are creating an association in your mind by rehearsing it (this is the same mechanism by which synchronicity cues work), and when you are absorbed and/or destabilized, your mind may look for that pattern and interpret it as present when it may not actually be. Research has shown that people that score highly on apophenia (the tendency to perceive meaningful patterns where none exists) also score highly on false positives for patterns that are not present, and also score highly on traits on the psychosis spectrum, although ordinary pattern noticing is not itself pathological (Blain et al., Grant et al.).

If you feel that synchronicity cues are making any of these worse (you find yourself compelled to scan your environment for them, you are unable to sleep, you are anxious, you become certain that random events are occurring to communicate something to you specifically, you have difficulty distinguishing observation from interpretation, etc.), you should deactivate them.

You can do this by simply ceasing to rehearse them, and saying, while fully awake, “Synchronicity is no longer to be used as a cue. I release this association and return coincidence to ordinary uncertainty.” Also remove it from your list of cues so that you stop rehearsing it. The statement expresses your decision; it does not prove the association has vanished immediately.

Reframing — changing the meaning without lying

Dishonest reframing declares that the problem was secretly good all along, so I prefer to ask myself questions that widen the meaning without lying, like: “What else could be true here?” or “What is this part trying to do for me?” or “How would my Nurturer reframe this?” or “How would my Protector reframe this?” or “How would my Leader reframe this?” and so on.

Perceptual positions — self, other, witness, universal heart

1. How do I feel about this from inside myself? 2. If I were inside of this other person, what might they be feeling or protecting? 3. If I were across the room watching this, what would I see? 4. From the universal heart, what serves truth, love, boundaries, and the good of everyone involved?

Don’t use these positions to excuse harm. Use them to get out of a prison of perception, to see from more than one angle.

Future pacing — let the future test the insight

1. Do some future pacing to make sure that the new insight holds, by imagining some future situations where the old behavior would have triggered.

If they appear, practice a new small behavior by setting up an implementation intention ("If...then..."):

The Swish, softened

2. Use a variation of the Swish Pattern from NLP, where instead of pushing out the old pattern (done mechanically, it can feel like an inner eviction), allowing it to stay there, just make sure that the old and the new pattern are both visible, feel the bodily sensations that arise, and compare what each future would actually require.

Parts integration, without pretending the conflict is solved

(What does one side want? What is the other side afraid of? What need sits under both? What is a 3rd option that meets each sides needs while not letting one side completely dominate?)

Deny legitimate signals

Override fear before asking what the fear protects

Recover memories

Manipulate anyone else

Convince myself an intuition is true

Do while in states of panic, destabilization, mania, “psychosis-like” states, being chemically overwhelmed, or too dissociated to reality-test

Make another person’s no feel like resistance

Making people feel spiritually inferior for disagreeing

Giving covert commands inside soft language

Creating urgency where time is needed

Bypassing consent by calling something “subconscious agreement.”

Using people’s trance, fatigue, attraction, shame, grief, or altered states to get compliance

Running the whole NLP sequence

Induce or contain. Gather attention, or stabilize first if you are already wide open.

Ask permission. Is it useful to work with this image, feeling, or pattern today?

Represent the pattern. How does it show up: image, voice, sensation, posture? How big? How close? What color? How does it move?

Ask what it protects. What is this trying to do for me?

Adjust the form of the pattern, gently (move it further away, turn down the volume, add space, change body posture, slow it down, etc.).

Introduce the three adults (Nurturer, Protector and Leader): the Nurturer warms, the Protector makes it safe, the Leader points a direction.

Anchor the useful state (heart, fingers, breath, body posture, etc.).

Future pace into a situation where this pattern used to be triggered: if the old cue shows up, what is the smallest new action?

Check the fit and the evidence: what changes in the body, is the response kind and doable, and what supports your interpretation of the situation beyond how it feels?

Exit altered state, come back to the room, and do one ordinary thing.

Appendix H: Demons, jinn, hostile presences, and “Unattached Burdens”

I’m going to come from experience here.

Sometimes, during self-hypnosis, meditation, lucid dreaming, loveyhuasca, grief, prayer, plant-medicine-adjacent practice, or a variety of other altered states of consciousness, you may encounter something you perceive to be a demon, a jinn, a parasitic energy, some other kind of dark intelligence, or even a terrifying archetype. Sometimes it comes as a voice. Sometimes as an image. It doesn’t feel like a simple emotion or a younger part, and it feels intrusive, hateful, seductive, mocking, or simply alien.

First and foremost, it doesn’t matter for the purposes of this guide whether they are literally demons or not. Maybe they are literal beings; maybe they are symbolic mind-forms, trauma in a frightening costume, dissociated energy, or ancestral and relational burdens. All that matters is the practical question: “What response makes me safer, clearer, more loving, more grounded, and less hooked?”

Start with the room, the body, and basic safety

So what do you do when a demon, or jinn, or other bad or intrusive entity shows up? Don’t reward it with instant certainty about what it is. Run the triage first: medical danger, environment, body, overload, and how open your mind has become. Open your eyes, feel your feet, name the room, lower the stimulation, leave hostile company, and stop adding prompts. Don’t go deeper, hunt for hidden truth, or debate what it is while you’re destabilized.

“Only what can be integrated is welcome right now. Anything that’s too much can wait. The adult in me is still here, and my body can go back to safety.”

If you feel like you’re in danger of hurting yourself or others, if you feel like you’re going psychotic and afraid, if you feel like you won’t be able to sleep afterwards, if you feel extremely paranoid, if you have chest pain, if you feel like you’re going to have a seizure, if you feel like you’re too hot in a serious way, if you feel like you’ve taken too much of something, or if you feel like you just can’t function in the world anymore, then the self-hypnosis session is over. Go get some real-world help.

A response check, not a verdict about what it is

If not, and you’re stable enough to stay present, check in with yourself as to what helps. Again, it doesn’t matter whether or not it’s literally a demon; this isn’t a test of what it is. Put your hand on your heart, if that feels welcome, take a comfortable breath, and keep the room available.

2. Internalize that you do not have to know what this is. Notice whether warmth or distance helps, and keep your boundary either way. Know that you are under no obligation to do whatever it is asking of you.

3. If you feel vulnerable, tightness in your throat, sadness, fear or a sense of trying to protect something, bring in your Nurturer. If it stays hostile or gets more frightening, then stop engaging with it and come back to your body and the room.

4. Again, you do not have to know where this is coming from. Ask yourself if this way of responding helps you become clearer, steadier, and less hooked. A protective part doesn’t have to show its fear quickly, and a comforting response doesn’t prove what it is either. You can use love and boundaries without deciding what it is first.

Do not fight from fear

The first impulse may be to fight it, banish it, hate it, show it I’m more powerful, argue with it, panic, become nothing but the threatened self, etc. Some traditions use prayers, mantras, protections, banishing and exorcism forms, and some people find them useful. The problem is, if you fight from fear…

…it becomes the center of your attention. When you hate it, you give it a hook in you. Pride gives it an opponent, and panic gives it your nervous system.

So the next time it shows up, simply say, “I see that there is no reason to hate or revile what I am experiencing. I see that there is no need to merge with or become what I am experiencing. I see that there is no need to obey what I am experiencing. I see that there is no need to defeat what I am experiencing from fear. I choose instead to return my attention to my loving awareness.”

A bodily boundary: compassion present, door closed

Secondly, feel free to maintain a bodily boundary and say to the presence “while compassion is present, the door is closed.”

This is especially important if the presence feels in any way hostile, cold, alien, parasitic, etc. It doesn’t respect my boundaries. In this case, don’t approach it with soft sentimental love, as though you were inviting it in for tea. Approach it with love while maintaining a boundary.

Sit up, ground your feet, straighten your spine, pull your shoulder blades back slightly so your chest is open but not exposed, feel the boundary of the skin around your torso and that this body has a perimeter, and simply say “While I recognize that there may be suffering here and I want all suffering to go back where it came from, the boundary of this skin is the boundary of an adult now. You don’t get to come in the house anymore.”

If it might be psychosis or destabilization

Thirdly, this exercise is assuming that you are having a symbolic experience of hostile presences which responds to grounding and love. That is very different from a state that becomes persistent, paranoid, sleepless, dangerous, or impossible to reality-test, which may be psychosis or another kind of destabilization.

If you feel like you are under attack for multiple days, are unable to sleep or function normally, are hearing commands, feel like you need to hurt yourself or somebody else, are going manic, are unable to communicate normally, or feel like you can’t tell the difference between symbolic experience and normal reality, get help immediately. This is not something to deal with in hypnosis.

As a general rule, if doing this makes you more loving, grounded, relational, honest, and functional, keep going, gently. If it makes you more Paranoid, sleepless, grandiose, isolated, scared, or unreal, stop going deeper and get support.

The cosmic-download humility test

Also, some of these presences or shadow forces or grandiose parts may respond not just by trying to scare you, but by trying to give you a sense that you are special, or trying to “download cosmic info” into you, or giving you a special mission that makes the dishes seem beneath you, etc. You can simply say “Thank you for the imagery. I don’t need a grand performance. Unless the info you have to download can become a simple, honest act of care tomorrow morning, like doing the dishes, cleaning my room, keeping a promise, apologizing, resting, eating or helping someone I love, I don’t need it.”

In other words, guidance worth keeping should make ordinary life, the dishes and the room included, more beautiful, honest, relational, humble, reliable, and useful to other people.

Don’t become an entity hobbyist

Finally, I recognize that some of you may be tempted to become hobbyists in regard to demons, jinns, hostile presences, Unattached Burdens, etc. The truth is, they all lead to the same practical training: can love stay present without giving up the boundary, and can your mind become harder to hook? Beyond that, I don’t really want you becoming hobbyists in this area.

Appendix J: A practical induction library

Practise: Preview, choose one purpose, decide whether to start. All ‘families’ can be light, eyes open, or replaced by no-trance contact. Monitor what happens (even if nothing seems to change) and decide on next action: move, imagine, change sensory channel, remain still, stop the sequence etc. Always do a complete waking return from induction.

NB If you cannot ‘see’ any images vividly, translate the metaphor into words, rhythm, spatial relations, touch, movement, knowing etc. The mind doesn’t owe anybody a movie.

Stretch and release

Focus on a feeling of support (and perhaps the position of one hand or foot). Either actually or in imagination stretch slightly and/or press into the support and then release. Notice any difference in feeling (even if nothing seems to change). Repeat this with no more than 3 areas of the body. Use the notion of ‘release’ to guide you through the sequence. Ask yourself which area, or which inner voice, wants attention, and what support is needed. Then bring back normal movement and return.

Supported floating

Notice where your weight is carried, and let the support carry 1% more of your effort, as if floating without losing contact, or keep the same weight and pressure. Notice what happens. It may help to fractionate, turning your attention toward normal awareness on the in-breath and toward the support on the out-breath. Tell yourself you're going to do this before you start. What becomes easier to hear? Keep the support, come back to the weight and firm contact you choose, and return.

Rhythmic breath or pulse

Try it with a natural rhythm; perhaps the rhythm of breathing or a slight hum in the throat. Try it with a more artificial rhythm, such as tapping a finger or listening to sounds outside. Even try it counting (silently) to yourself, or even with no rhythm at all. Say the words 'here, and here again' over and over, noticing where your attention lands in between, then stop the rhythm. Notice the first quiet beat - do not try and make your mind blank. This might bring a bit more clarity to what word, feeling, need or action is coming up. Then let your normal rhythm come back, and return.

Unwinding object

A quick exercise for when one concern has several strands. Imagine yarn unwinding, bubbles settling, or knots placed where you can see them beside you. When you've placed them all, take a minute to look at them all (without changing them, though you could label them if needed, by saying a word or two). Count only the strands you actually set down; nothing is erased. Which one needs warmth, protection, or action? Now keep one useful strand, put the others somewhere you can see them, and return.

Sensory journey

Listen to the sounds of the room you are currently in and feel your body. Now imagine yourself walking somewhere, where do you want to go? As you walk, listen to the sounds of your footsteps and take in your surroundings. What texture are the objects you pass? What landmarks do you see? Now that you've collected enough attention, imagine the scenery changing until you are in a place where whoever or whatever needs to speak can speak. Or you can just cut straight to the chase if you want. Notice a detail without giving it a hidden meaning, the mystery is how the scene develops, so don't make it into a "what are they going to do to you?" kind of thing. When you're ready to finish, imagine walking back the way you came and close the space.

Gradual wave

Begin with the smallest area possible that is neutral. Sense what is already there, and imagine warmth, steadiness or attention radiating outward to the next area, which should still feel comfortable. Continue this, pausing and sensing in each new area, or continue with the original area, only. Notice what changes, without claiming any medical repair. Does the body want contact, space, words, or ordinary care? Allow the image to fade, sense the whole body, the contact points, and return.

Care workshop

First get ready for some patient, unhurried care: time, place, tools and boundaries. Let the signal, the feeling or the younger state come only as close as is welcome. Be careful to not use language which makes you fragmented. Ask before you respond, wait, reconnect only where that’s welcome, rest, and see again. If you have an adult part which can do this or borrow a function from someone else, let that help. You decide the words, the pace and what you want to do. Aim for “good as you,” not an erased history. Finally, close the workspace. Say that you are whole, an adult and come back.

Resource embodiment

Choose a quality you understand, like warmth, a boundary, steadiness, curiosity or dignity. Imagine your posture, voice or attention with just 1% more access to it, or, if you’d rather, simply observe it. Notice what happens. Repeat a few times, to strengthen your access to it, not to become someone else. How would that quality meet the situation you’re in today? Finally keep the quality and one useful action, let go of the role, say to yourself "I am myself", and return.

No-trance inner contact

Observable pacing: keep the eyes open, notice where the practice is taking place and on what day, notice the feet, read something, write something, notice that one is still relatively normally aware.

Invitation: choose a question and keep it in mind, do not specifically focus or narrow the awareness further.

Genuine choice: answer the question or write it down, write that one does not know, rest, change the question, ask someone else, stop the practice, etc.

Autonomous signal: write down any word, sensation, impulse, objection, or silence that comes, without taking it as proof.

Deepener: none, full alertness isn’t a lesser version of the practice.

Handoff: have the adult part of yourself answer the question in any way, preferably in writing or by taking an action.

Integration/exit: reality test the autonomous signal and do one small action based on that, end the practice (no special exit is needed since no state was achieved that one needs to exit from).
